items.user: We distribute torque tools in Europe. Which sub-types here are best for workshop service kits, and do you support OEM packaging?

data.reply:
For workshop service kits, the most suitable sub-types in this category are typically:
- Socket tool sets, such as the 94-piece metric socket tool set, for broad service coverage
- Ratchet handles, including 72-tooth reversible and flex-head types, for daily workshop use
- Torque wrenches for controlled fastening in service and maintenance work
- Digital torque adapters if you want to add torque verification capability to existing tool programs
- Fastening accessories to complete kit configurations

Based on your market, a practical workshop kit program would usually combine a socket set, one or more ratchet handles, and a torque control item.

On OEM packaging: this category description confirms these tools are intended for export-ready product programs, but OEM packaging support is not explicitly confirmed on this page. If OEM packaging is required, the best next step is to send an RFQ with your target product mix, branding requirements, and estimated volume so the team can confirm packaging options.

items.user: We want to build a mid-range automotive aftermarket assortment for distributors. Which products should we start with?

data.reply:
For a mid-range automotive aftermarket assortment aimed at distributors, a practical starting mix would be:

1. Torque tools
- Core for workshop maintenance programs
- Suitable where repeat-use durability matters

2. Ratchets
- A staple line for service and repair assortments
- Pairs naturally with socket programs

3. Socket systems
- Important for reducing fit inconsistency across the range
- Good foundation for distributor resale

4. Extraction tools
- Useful for automotive service applications and broadening the maintenance offer

5. Service kits
- Helps create ready-to-sell assortments for common workshop needs

6. Workshop-ready packaging
- Supports distributor resale and more coherent shelf or catalog presentation

A balanced entry program would usually combine torque tools, ratchets, socket systems, and selected service kits first, then expand with extraction and broader maintenance tools.

NorthForge supports fastening, torque-control, extraction, and maintenance-tool programs for workshop use, distributor resale, and branded service assortments. If you want, the next step is to outline an RFQ around your target assortment structure, branding needs, and channel focus.

items.user: We also need private-label packaging and stable workshop durability. Which product best covers torque-critical service work, and what should we confirm before RFQ?

data.reply:
For torque-critical service work, the best-fit starting product is torque tools. In this application, they are the most directly aligned with torque-control needs and recurring workshop use.

Given your private-label packaging and durability focus, the main points to confirm before RFQ are:
1. Product scope
- Which torque tools you want included in the initial assortment
- Whether they will be sold as individual items or in service kits

2. Workshop-use expectations
- Required durability level for recurring workshop use
- Any specific concerns from your channel around tool life or consistency

3. Packaging requirements
- Private-label packaging format
- Whether you need workshop-ready packaging for distributor resale
- Branding and assortment presentation requirements

4. Assortment structure
- Whether torque tools will be paired with ratchets, socket systems, or service kits
- Target range depth for distributors

5. Channel focus
- Distributor resale only, workshop supply, or branded service assortment programs

NorthForge supports torque tools, service kits, and workshop-ready packaging for automotive aftermarket programs, so this is a good basis for an RFQ. If you want, the next step is to prepare an RFQ outline for torque tools plus private-label packaging.
